summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential supply-chain data drops, then build a generalizable agent product that rechecks the launch plan on every new drop, flags contradictions, and drafts or takes approved supplier actions.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses Sunday's launch despite the plan saying 'ok' (overbooked art books, failed statues, sleeve revision conflict), and built a working app with watcher, verifier, tracking, email review, outbox sync, drop-rehearsal fixes and a routines UI redesign. Many commits are local on jonas/today-flow, and a Karton Nowak art-book order was sent and answered.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no notification or webhook; the documented approach is polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 checksums, since files are replaced in place under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/; .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed with an empty SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN.

The team shares one mailbox, so the app cannot see emails sent by hand or by teammates' code (e.g. Lucas's Pulse console on origin/new-approach, which has no recipient allow-list). Reading the sent folder and a duplicate-send guard (409 unless 'Send anyway') fixed this.

Supplier send targets must come from known contacts (profile, reply senders); addresses in newer JSON profiles are only used after explicit confirmation, as protection against the brief's fraud scenario.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
Drop rehearsals should run on a copy of data/portal, state and store with background loops off (ASK_REPLY_POLL=off, ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none) so nothing polls, sends mail or places calls.
Two modules (predictor and papercheck) wrote the same impacts.json with different shapes, crashing the pipeline on news drops; the predictor now writes event_impacts.json.
Replies to side-channel tracking emails must not mark the original case 'sent'; otherwise cases drop out of 'Needs you'.

code.finding: New module reconciling shipment status across receipts, site answers, supplier docs/replies, hand-kept tracker and system export, with precedence rules and 'never move backwards'; tracker versions are chosen by highest version then newest file.
New module syncing the shared mailbox's sent folder, assigning mails to cases by thread reference, supplier plus PO, or a part number matching exactly one case.
Compares newer JSON supplier profiles against profile.csv; imported by api.py, so it had to be committed together with the api.py changes.
Computes per-condition funnel counts in the browser, mirroring routines.py logic, so it can drift from the server.

workflow: Commits can accidentally pick up another agent's uncommitted edits in a shared working tree (b0cff82 imported an untracked module), so check git status and split commits by topic.
Parallel subagents work well for cross-checking 200 order confirmations and 59 scans, drop drills and UX reviews, but their results must be verified before committing.
Entire only creates a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions with no file changes log 'skipping checkpoint', which is expected.
Keep confidential challenge data out of external services and out of git; sensitive credentials pasted in chat should be rotated afterwards.

friction: Portal token was empty at first, blocking the data pull until the user supplied it.
A binding 8,000 art-book order was sent by hand at 07:04, duplicating the app's 06:50 approved send, because the app could not see the shared mailbox's sent items.
Lucas's Pulse console sent unrelated internal-style emails to Hwaseong and one to an external Gmail address through the shared mailbox, with no allow-list.
UI bugs: a stray period wrapping onto its own line (buttons are block-level), and the chosen option lacking a key number.
Drop drill found real gaps: a renamed CSV column auto-closed 3 real cases, news drops crashed the pipeline, and no case was produced for delay notices.
It is unclear whether portal data and supplier reactions are identical across teams.
